summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a man with relapsed multiple myeloma, end-stage renal disease on dialysis, chronic hemolytic anemia, and dementia, was readmitted with altered mental status, lethargy, and subjective fever one day after discharge from a prior hospitalization for a pathological left femur fracture. He had recently undergone femoral resection and hip hemiarthroplasty and was recovering at a nursing facility. On admission, he reported headache and left calf pain, though imaging ruled out DVT. Chest imaging showed worsening bilateral lung opacities and pleural effusions, consistent with aspiration-related pneumonitis, likely due to oropharyngeal dysphagia confirmed by a video swallow study showing trace aspiration. He was treated with broad-spectrum antibiotics, and blood cultures remained negative. A Dobhoff tube was placed for enteral nutrition due to aspiration risk. Delirium persisted but was attributed to multifactorial causes including infection, metabolic stress, and underlying cognitive impairment. MRI of the brain and spine showed no acute abnormalities but confirmed chronic changes and stable myeloma involvement. He gradually improved, became afebrile, and repeat swallow study showed no overt aspiration, allowing initiation of thickened oral intake. He was discharged to extended care rehab for continued dialysis, wound care, rehabilitation, and monitoring.
